# Facilitation Architecture

This file is the index. The cards live in `resources/`, one file per stage.

Choosing starts from what the room owes: a shared problem before divergence, a spread of options before convergence, a decision before planning, a plan before the room leaves. Read the stage that matches the debt, then the one card that fits the people and the clock.

When two cards fit, take the one whose failure you can recognize in this room. A method's failure mode is what it costs when it half-works, and a facilitator who can name it will see it coming.

Running one without flattening the room: say what the group leaves with, give the silence its timer, and never fill a pause longer than the instruction. The steps are beats, not a script; the fix is the sentence to say when the beat goes wrong.

Rules that hold across every card:

- Name the deliverable before anyone starts. A group that does not know what it walks out with will produce a conversation.
- Silence is part of the method. Protect it with a timer and do not narrate it.
- One exercise, one debt. Do not stack two methods to fix a room that needs a decision.
- When the room goes flat, read the failure line before inventing a new intervention.
- An inventory-only card's steps are written for this deck from the method's public definition; the card says so. Do not present them as a source script.
